intent: A CSV-to-Parquet normaliser for three vendor feeds. Adapters must stay ignorant of the output format, the domain must stay ignorant of the ORM, and no rule may be believed to block without actually denying a write.

units.owns: the normalised row schema and the VendorAdapter protocol
must_not_know: any vendor's name, dialect or quirks
units.reason: Seams are settled before anything is written against them.

units.owns: one module per vendor, each implementing VendorAdapter
units.reason: Adapters are written against a settled contract.
The writer sees only the settled schema.

units.owns: argument parsing and the run pipeline
units.reason: The entry point is wired last, once both sides exist.

rules.title: Adapters must not import the writer
rules.rationale: An adapter that knows the output format cannot be reused for another one.

rules.title: The domain must not import the ORM
rules.rationale: A domain type that imports the ORM cannot be tested without a database.

rules.title: Command handlers live under src/cli/

authority.source: the declared unit layout in ruleset.units

rules.rationale: A handler outside the entry-point unit is a second entry point nobody documented.

rules.title: No credential files in the tree
rules.rationale: A committed credential is compromised the moment the repo is cloned.

rules.title: No bare except
rules.rationale: A bare except also catches KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit.

rules.title: Every public function carries type hints

authority.source: PEP 484; the repo's own mypy.ini strict block

rules.rationale: An untyped seam is a seam no checker can hold to its contract.

rules.title: No unused imports
rules.rationale: An unused import is a dependency the module does not actually have.

rules.title: Public symbols carry a docstring
rules.rationale: An undocumented public seam is a contract nobody wrote down.

rules.title: No bare print() in library code
rules.rationale: A library that prints cannot have its output redirected by its caller.

rules.title: Handlers orchestrate; they do not decide
rules.rationale: Business logic in a handler is logic that cannot be exercised without the CLI.

check.asks: Does this handler make a normalisation decision instead of delegating one?

rules.title: Cross-unit seams are Protocols, not concrete classes
rules.rationale: A concrete base class at a seam couples both sides to an inheritance tree.

check.asks: Is this seam declared as a Protocol, or as a concrete class both sides must inherit?
